strongest_accepted_preservation.evidence: 8/13 teacher atoms, all 7/7 frozen control atoms retained, e6.a recovered, full page-ceiling fraction
strongest_accepted_preservation.constraint: Accepted lexical threshold remains frozen and is not retuned post hoc.

rejected_generalizations.reason: No frozen SPARK threshold met precision>=0.95 and recall>=0.05.
No safe SPARK threshold; FOBIE held-out relation recall 4/153 despite 100% sentence unit coverage.

evidence: AMR abstracts away from syntactic realization and represents predicate-argument semantics as a graph.
AMR similarity work shows graph structure can support semantic comparison, while symbolic Smatch remains the standard auditable structural metric.
Cross-domain AMR parsing research identifies word/concept distribution shift as a central domain risk and reports modern general-domain parsers around 0.597-0.669 Smatch on the Bio OOD benchmark.

AMR-3 LDC2020T02 documents general-domain sources only; Bio-AMR is separately used as a 500-instance biomedical OOD test set, so Bio-AMR is eligible as independent domain-fidelity evidence for an AMR-3-trained parser.
A public Git mirror pins the original Bio-AMR v0.8 test bytes at AMR-World@802923ae6c7376a9930e93ce52cd6b9faf43c411, blob 7e816eb86104fa6c07d8eff9f9c6abc84bae2898.
amrlib parse_xfm_bart_large v0.1.0 reports 83.7 Smatch on AMR-3 and is publicly released under the MIT-licensed amrlib stack.
strengths: Direct graph representation of semantic concepts and roles rather than local surface tuples.
Parser fidelity can be independently measured on biomedical gold AMR before any EXTRACT use.
SPARK can separately test whether graph similarity is safe enough for proposition redundancy.
risks: General-domain parser may fail under scientific domain shift.
Smatch is structural graph overlap and may not perfectly represent semantic equivalence.
Smatch v1.0.4 internally reseeds its hill-climbing search from system entropy unless explicitly intercepted, so deterministic validation requires a frozen seed wrapper.
Neural AMR parsing introduces a learned component and GPU execution cost.

evidence: Question decomposition can improve complementary evidence retrieval on multi-hop RAG benchmarks.
2025 fact-checking research documents decomposition error/noise and sensitivity to atomicity.
Verifier-preferred decomposition can improve downstream verification but introduces a generation policy and verifier interaction.
strengths: Could expose missing evidence obligations directly.
risks: Adds generative decomposition before a directly gold-validatable semantic graph route is exhausted.
Atomicity and decontextualization choices create another model-controlled semantic bottleneck.
External validation is less cleanly separable from downstream verifier behavior.

selected_validation.purpose: Externally validate both scientific-domain AMR parser fidelity and graph-similarity redundancy safety before any AMR-derived certificate is allowed inside EXTRACT.

execution.gpu_requirement: one CUDA-visible GPU is sufficient; parser must bind to cuda:0 only
execution.external_network_use: Only pinned source/model/data acquisition needed for this validation is allowed.

smatch.deterministic_reseed_rule: For each AMR pair, derive seed = first 64 bits of SHA256(canonical pair identity). Temporarily replace smatch.random.seed with a wrapper that always calls the captured original random.seed(seed), so every internal no-argument reseed is deterministic; restore the original seed function after scoring.

parser_model.identity_rule: Workflow must verify parser release asset size and published MD5 before extraction, compute SHA256 of the downloaded parser tarball, acquire the facebook/bart-large tokenizer only from revision 22fa33834dccc11df99c4fc5fcc96c67f806dfdb into a local directory, pass that local path as tok_name_or_path, and persist parser tarball SHA256 plus tokenizer manifest SHA256 in the report.

tokenizer.acquisition: Download tokenizer files from this exact Hugging Face revision into an ephemeral local directory and pass that directory as tok_name_or_path to amrlib. Network resolution from moving main is forbidden.

external_validation_sets.source: SemEval-2017 Task 9 / AMR-ISI public corpus, pinned via AMR-World mirror
external_validation_sets.identity_rule: Workflow must acquire exactly the pinned AMR-World mirror commit/blob and persist SHA256 of the file before scoring.

leakage_audit.evidence: AMR-3 LDC2020T02 documents general-domain source datasets; published OOD evaluations treat Bio-AMR as separate from AMR-3 and evaluate AMR-3-trained parsers on Bio.

pair_construction.positive: unordered distinct-text span pairs in the same proposition cluster
pair_construction.negative: unordered distinct-text span pairs from different proposition clusters within the same topic
pair_construction.negative_sampling: deterministically retain at most 5 negatives per positive by SHA256(pair identity), separately per split
pair_construction.topic_split: Sort topic IDs by SHA256(topic_id); first half calibration, second half held-out evaluation.

external_validation_sets.calibration_rule: Choose the lowest graph-similarity threshold in the frozen grid with precision >=0.95 and recall >=0.05. If none exists, validation is rejected.

graph_similarity.definition: Parse both propositions once with the pinned amrlib parser, remove metadata, and compute standard Smatch v1.0.4 F1. Invalid/unparseable graphs score 0.0.
graph_similarity.deterministic_alignment: For every pair, derive a pair-specific seed from SHA256(canonical pair identity) and intercept Smatch's internal random.seed() calls so they always reseed to that pair seed; retain standard iteration_num=5 and restore random.seed after scoring.
graph_similarity.parser_cache: Parse every unique SPARK text once; reuse the graph for all pairs.
graph_similarity.bio_scoring: Score all 500 pinned Bio-AMR predictions against gold with deterministic per-example Smatch; report aggregate corpus precision/recall/F1 from summed matching/test/gold triples and valid prediction fraction. Invalid predictions contribute zero matches and remain in the denominator.

gate_logic.bio_amr_pass: aggregate corpus Smatch F1 >=0.60 AND valid prediction fraction >=0.98
gate_logic.spark_pass: safe calibration threshold exists AND held-out precision>=0.90 AND recall>=0.05 AND false-positive-rate<=0.02
gate_logic.AMR_GRAPH_CERTIFICATE_PARTIAL: exactly one of bio_amr_pass or spark_pass
gate_logic.AMR_GRAPH_CERTIFICATE_REJECTED: neither passes OR no safe SPARK calibration threshold exists
gate_logic.note: No EXTRACT teacher label, teacher atom, or EXTRACT benchmark may participate in parser selection, threshold selection, or verdict.

decision_boundary.if_validated: Checkpoint exact parser tarball SHA256, pinned tokenizer revision/manifest SHA256, pinned Bio-AMR mirror commit/blob/file SHA256, SPARK file SHA256, amrlib/smatch identities, selected threshold, run/artifact/report identities, then open a separate EXTRACT design for substituting graph similarity into the accepted dynamic-swap/page-preservation/top-24 architecture.
decision_boundary.if_partial_or_rejected: Do not tune parser model, tokenizer revision, beam count, Smatch deterministic reseed rule, threshold grid, or Bio-AMR/SPARK gates using EXTRACT results. Reassess claim/question decomposition, UCCA, or another materially different teacher-blind evidence representation.
decision_boundary.never: Do not start Wave 7B, change production EXTRACT/VERIFY, retrain/fine-tune the AMR parser, use EXTRACT teacher labels, emit RDF/ontology output, or change EXTRACT output for semantic-control.

independent_review_boundary.action: After this design is durable and before implementation, re-read the review capsule and consume only an exact-SHA review if one exists; do not block indefinitely if none exists.

rules: Do not alter EXTRACT science, graph representation, thresholds, or output shape for semantic-control.
Do not emit RDF, ontology-native output, or SemanticObservationV1.
Integration remains downstream of a future accepted EXTRACT output checkpoint.

next_safe_action: CI-lock this tokenizer-pinned design hotfix. Before implementation, re-read the independent-review capsule for any checkpoint explicitly tied to the exact durable hotfix SHA. If none exists, implement only the external AMR_GRAPH_REDUNDANCY_CERTIFICATE_VALIDATION_V1 harness/workflow and run no EXTRACT teacher benchmark.
